data_fields.name: aggression
data_fields.donor_constant: int per model; wait = randf(max(1, game_speed*3/4 - aggression))

data_fields.name: offscreen_noatk_factor
data_fields.donor_constant: global 0.5, per-model override; chance *= (1 - factor) when off screen

data_fields.name: target_window_max
data_fields.donor_constant: 9999 (distance window upper bound; lower bound 0 exclusive)

data_fields.name: run_gap
data_fields.donor_constant: 150 (run when x gap > 150 and run animation exists)

data_fields.name: back_off_gap
data_fields.donor_constant: 80 (step back only when opponent within 80; cap at target +/- 80)

data_fields.name: back_off_chance
data_fields.donor_constant: (rand32() & 3) non-zero, i.e. 3 in 4 if low bits uniform

best_idea: A victim's hit clears its own attack cooldown, and an attacker's cooldown is cleared when its target blocks and cut while its target attacks or jumps, so fights stay fast without a separate aggro table.
decision_why: Take the target rule (nearest in front; a non-vulnerable pick is replaced by any later candidate), the cooldown relief and the victim reset. Do not port the crowd term: it is dead for normal, upper and duck attacks because the clamp forces chance to 1, and MAX_ATTACKERS = 3 must be an engine rule, not a donor chance term.
acceptance: A server test with one player and five hostile enemies at x = 100..300 asserts the picked target is the nearest enemy in front, that a non-vulnerable pick is replaced by a later candidate, that a landed hit sets the victim's nextAttack to 0 on that tick, and that no more than 3 enemies hold ATTACKING at once.
